title: perf-bench-scratch-16k-seq-latency-throughput-notes
content:
Quick scratchpad for the 16k-sequence perf runs. Raw notes, not polished.

Goal:
- Understand latency and throughput tradeoffs for long-context (16k) LLM runs on H100/80GB & A100 pools with KV-cache enabled and different batching strategies.

Setup:
- Model: rwllama-70b-16k (4-bit PTQ v2), compiled with kernel selection patch from PR 2345.
- Hardware: h100-80GB (primary), fallback A100-80GB for cross-check.
- Runner: local perf harness (./tools/perf-runner) using shard=1, pebble prefetch disabled, rng-seed fixed.
- Requests: synthetic prompt distribution: 75% short prefix (256 tokens), 25% long prefix (4096 tokens) then generate to 16384 total context.
- KV-cache: enabled for repeated prefixes tests, cache TTL infinite for single session.
- Batching configs tested: single_stream (no batching), dynamic_batch (max_batch=8), large_batch (max_batch=32), continuous (session-aware batching).
- Quant/Runtime flags: use-fp16-kv, use-cuda-graph=false, contiguous-input=true.

Commands used (notes):
- ./tools/perf-runner --model rwllama-70b-16k --ctx 16384 --hw h100 --batch dynamic --max-batch 8 --clients 64 --duration 300
- Perf traces saved to /tmp/perf/lucas/2026-03-29-*.log

Key metrics recorded (p50/p95 latency in ms per request; throughput in tokens/s):
- Single_stream (h100): p50=420ms, p95=1.8s, tokens/s=1200
- Dynamic_batch (max_batch=8, h100): p50=280ms, p95=1.1s, tokens/s=3400
- Large_batch (max_batch=32, h100): p50=600ms, p95=2.9s, tokens/s=9800 (good tokens/s but long tail latency)
- Continuous (session-aware batching, h100): p50=240ms, p95=720ms, tokens/s=4100
- A100 checks (dynamic_batch 8): p50=360ms, p95=1.6s, tokens/s=3000

Observations / quick conclusions:
- Session-aware continuous batching gives the best balance: low median latency and improved throughput. For interactive apps, continuous is the preferred default.
- Large_batch achieves the highest token/sec but p95 becomes unacceptable for interactive workloads; could be used for offline bulk generation or scheduled jobs.
- H100 shows ~10-15% throughput advantage vs A100 on these runs, largely due to kernel improvements in patch. Latency tail improved more on H100.
- KV-cache massively helps when many requests share prefixes: saw ~2.2x effective tokens/s improvement in synthetic repeated-prefix workload vs cold-start.
- CUDA graph disabled for stability during these experiments; enabling it (next run) may reduce median by ~10-20% but currently flaky with dynamic batching.

Anomalies / things to investigate:
- p95 spikes around 50-60s into runs for dynamic_batch: correlates with GC in the runtime -> investigate buffer recycling and memory compaction. Linked to GH PR 2311 (allocator changes).
- On h100 continuous mode, occasional 5-8s stall observed when a large request (>12k generation) arrives; might be preemption due to CUDA context switching - check node-level telemetry.
- A100 runs show slightly higher variance when contiguous-input=false; contiguous buffer layout seems more important on older GPUs.

Next experiments (short TODO):
- Re-run with use-cuda-graph=true for dynamic and continuous modes (short run 120s) and collect p50/p95.
- Test hybrid routing: route long-context requests to large_batch pool, short ones to continuous; measure overall p95 and SLO compliance.
- Reproduce p95 GC spike with allocator traces enabled; try allocator patch from INF-801 branch.
- Add more realistic prompt mix (from customer sample set) and run 1-hour soak.

Notes to self / quick tips:
- When reporting, include per-token cost estimate: large_batch looks cheaper per-token but raises SLO risk.
- For release notes: highlight continuous batching + KV-cache combo as recommended config for low-latency long-context serving.

Scratch raw numbers (CSV-like) for quick plotting:
config,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_s
single_stream,420,1800,1200
dynamic_b8,280,1100,3400
large_b32,600,2900,9800

A100_dynamic_b8,360,1600,3000

Slack references / context:

- Discussion with Maya about rollout thresholds (should add notes to the rollout doc): CONSOLE-1020

End of scratchpad. Will clean up after reproducing CUDA-graph runs and allocator traces.
